clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A nurse is preparing to access a client's hemodialysis central venous catheter. Which infection-prevention action is required each time the catheter is accessed?

options.A: Scrub the catheter hub with an appropriate antiseptic after removing the cap and before accessing the catheter.
options.B: Access the hub without disinfection when the catheter dressing remains clean, dry, and intact.
options.C: Use routine clean handling without aseptic catheter-access technique when the client has no fever or local redness.
options.D: Disinfect the hub at insertion and omit repeat disinfection during later dialysis sessions.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC's current dialysis bloodstream-infection prevention Core Interventions instruct staff to scrub hemodialysis catheter hubs with an appropriate antiseptic after the cap is removed and before catheter access, and to perform this every time the catheter is accessed or disconnected. CDC also requires adherence to aseptic technique during catheter connection and disconnection. A clean dressing does not remove the need for hub disinfection, and disinfection is not a one-time insertion step.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Prevent hemodialysis catheter-related bloodstream infection by disinfecting the catheter hub with an appropriate antiseptic before every access.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Best Practices for Bloodstream Infection Prevention in Dialysis Setting
semantic_correction.source_version_date: March 29, 2024; current CDC dialysis-safety guidance accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Core Interventions — Catheter hub disinfection: scrub catheter hubs with an appropriate antiseptic after the cap is removed and before accessing; perform every time the catheter is accessed or disconnected. Catheter/vascular access care observations — assess adherence to aseptic technique when connecting and disconnecting catheters
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Hemodialysis catheter hubs must be disinfected with an appropriate antiseptic after cap removal and before access every time the catheter is accessed or disconnected, using aseptic technique.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed 'only' distractor cueing, kept all choices focused on catheter-access technique, and anchored the answer to CDC's explicit every-access hub-disinfection requirement.

audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — aseptic invasive-device care
audit_findings_append.finding: The original construct was clinically correct but contained absolute-word distractors. The revised item directly tests CDC's every-access hub-disinfection requirement with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reproduces the CDC catheter-hub disinfection sequence required before each access.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Dressing condition does not substitute for hub disinfection before catheter access.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Hemodialysis catheter connection/disconnection requires aseptic technique regardless of fever or local redness.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. CDC requires repeat hub disinfection every time the catheter is accessed or disconnected.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches the explicit CDC every-access requirement.
cueing_check: All four choices describe catheter-access handling of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
